# Independent audit: actual smoothed normal Hessians

Audited `candidate 8bc6ff090380166a`.
Result: PASS, with its stated hypotheses and limitations. No repair requested.

The checks were substantive rather than an appeal to a formal Hessian:

1. For m_t=(N+tD).(w-Y)/Gamma(u+tv), Gamma=1,
   m'_0=k and m''_0=-2 gamma k-eta m. Thus the actual normalized kernel
   argument has the stated derivatives; the source buffer b is fixed after
   normalization. The radial normal direction gives both k=eta=0.
2. Since integral m psi/h=A-bS and actual full-normal stationarity gives
   integral k psi/h=0, the correction is +(bS-A)eta. The sign is positive
   for the outward kernel. This computation works equally for b=0.
3. On a proper section the central hinge trace is full k^2. At a supporting
   facet its central trace is k^2/2. For example, on the body-positive side
   a positive t loses a small triangular integral only when k<0, giving
   the one-sided k_-^2 trace; reversing t and averaging gives k^2/2. Thus
   the full/half convention and the stated one-sided signs are correct.
4. The lower hinge has a plus sign and the upper hinge a minus sign. For an
   outside support, the lower section is inward and the upper outward, so
   lower-minus-upper is nonnegative. The signs reverse at inside support.
   The section homotheties have scale tending to1 and justify the weak
   measure comparison without assuming a bounded scaled roof.
5. Multiplication by h makes h(bS-A)eta vanish on the compact actual
   sequence. Proper sections cancel, leaving the stated simultaneous PSD
   transition measure on the limiting supporting facets. A finite moment
   matrix gives simultaneity for all variations.
6. The interval-footprint record has weight1 on 0<g<1 and weight1/2 at
   actual positive-area equality plateaus. On 0<tau<1 its weak limit is1;
   at tau=0 or1 it can retain any additional weak transition information.
   In particular replacing chi by 1_(0<tau<1) would lose valid data.

The proof uses fiberwise section and facet measures, so sampled boundary
bases are not discarded through ambient-null surface arguments. The
conclusion is capwise normal second-order necessity. It does not assert
body C2 regularity, pointwise inside/outside domination, or numerical
Gamma_d/k payment.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
